commits.message:
Take the responder's validity and deadlines from the committee's L1 clock

The availability responder read Date.now() for its transaction's
validity window and for every due, expired and deadline decision. A
committee member whose wall clock drifted from the chain's could give up
on a response it could still publish, or build one outside the window
the ledger accepts.

The committee now keeps an L1 clock: the newest tip slot its follower
observed plus the monotonic time since, never decreasing. Every boundary
read observes the tip, and until one has, a step reports that it is
awaiting the scan. The responder's deadline checks, the transaction's
validity window and a check after the build all read that clock. A
publication's inclusive upper bound is the response deadline plus one,
and settling an Active tranche starts at the deadline. When the tip lags
too far for any valid interval, the step reports pending and tries again
on the next tick.

In promise mode valid_to still follows the promise network clock, so
the promise TTL rule holds while the L1 clock lags. Leases and journal
timestamps stay on the wall clock, since other processes read them. The
SDK runner's wall-clock deadline guard is no longer used: both modes
fence the preparation scope at the deadline on the L1 clock, so signing
still stops once it passes.
Call the forced-order spend a close-out in fault-proof tests

Prove a same-block missing output index with its NoIdx family

An input or reference input naming an output index past the end of a
producer committed by the same block is also absent from the event's
pre-state ledger, so the ledger-absence family found it at the same event
and, ranking first in catalogue order, was selected whenever the
predecessor ledger was available. Per the owner ruling of 2026-11-15
(decision 0010), the classifier now ranks nonExistentInputNoIndex ahead of
nonExistentInput and referenceInputNoIdx ahead of noReferenceInput, as an
owner-ruled promotion beside the existing doubleWithdraw one. Every other
family keeps its catalogue order.

The NoIdx detectors now emit a finding only when both the naming
transaction and the producer are accepted, matching what steps 01 and 03
bind; a finding naming a TxIsInvalid transaction could never be proved.

Tests: with the predecessor ledger present, both fields select the NoIdx
family and its four-step route mints the proof on the emulator; an absent
input with no same-block producer stays with the ledger-absence family; a
TxIsInvalid producer or spender yields no NoIdx finding; the Preprod-stack
drill check now asserts the full catalogue selects each staged category.

Pay the deployment's minimum fee in every drill transaction a replay accepts

The history, withdrawn-input, withdrawal-split and transaction-fault
fixtures built their transactions at fee zero. A Preprod stack's node
commits a nonzero fee schedule into every header, so those controls and
honest successors replayed rejected, and faults that were not about the
fee were classified as minFee instead of their own family.

Each of these builders now prices its transaction through
buildAtJourneyMinFee from the predecessor header's schedule, taking the
fee out of its change output. The minFee fault alone still pays nothing,
since that fee is the fault it carries.

Tests build the fixtures on a predecessor whose header commits the
schedule from the node environment example, and check that controls
replay accepted and faults are rejected and proved. The history fixture
test runs in CI with the other watcher journeys that need no devnet.

Pay the deployment's minimum fee in every forced-order transaction

The transaction a forced-order fixture places in its L1 order paid no fee,
so on a stack whose nodes charge a nonzero L2 fee its valid control replayed
as E_MIN_FEE and the drill stopped at the forced order inclusion interval.
It now pays the minimum fee its size prices under the retained
predecessor's schedule, the schedule the block's replay applies.

Normal journey controls and the Plutus mint journey priced their fees with
two copies of the same loop; all three now share one helper.

The forced-order tests build their predecessor with the fee schedule a
Preprod stack's node commits, read from the node's environment example.

Alert when the watcher finds a block no installed family proves

A header whose latest decision is unprovable because no installed
fault-proof family proves its finding (an unregistered finding, or a
category the deployment does not install) now raises the
proof_family_coverage_gap alert, one subject per header. Being a
non-informational alert it holds readiness, as an unprovable header must,
while the bridge keeps classifying and proving later headers. A decision
waiting on its predecessor's context raises nothing.

The alert clears without an operator when a later decision of the header
is not such a gap, or when the header merges, is removed, or leaves the
observed queue, rollbacks included. The merged-header recorder, which
already sees each header's release and latest decision, drives it.

Adds the MidgardWatcherProofFamilyCoverageGap alert rule and its runbook
entry.

Classify a forced rejection naming a coordinate the transaction lacks

A forced leaf's rejection reason names coordinates the block producer
chose: a field index, an item index, an input source kind, a script item
kind, a decode class. A claimed coordinate the transaction does not have
is a classification outcome, never a classifier error, but several
detectors indexed straight into the transaction with it and threw, which
failed the header's classification.

Detectors now open claimed coordinates through one seam
(evidence/claimed-coordinate.ts) that returns undefined outside the
transaction; the detector then reports no finding of its own family for
that claim. Only the claim is forgiven: a field preimage that does not
decode for any other reason, or authenticated material that disagrees
with its commitment, still throws.

When the complete replay finds nothing provable, the header classifier
adds one forced-claim-coordinate-absent detection per rejected forced leaf
whose claimed coordinate is certainly absent. No family is registered for
it, so such a block classifies as an unprovable gap rather than healthy,
and it never displaces a finding a family proves.

The new watcher-journey suite classifies 62 wrongful forced rejections
against one valid native forced transaction, covering absent, negative
and largest coordinates for every arm that names one, and is wired into
the node-tools journey CI step.

A rejection naming the reference script of an output that carries none
(OutputReferenceScriptMalformed, NodeLimit, DepthLimit, or
PlutusScriptUndecodable on an output) was not prepared, because the
detector required a reference script at the output. Such an output now
binds the empty item and closes no-fault at step 04, the twin of the
on-chain bind's language -1 arm, so the rejection is contradicted on
chain. The registered-chain lifecycle test runs the forced Malformed claim
at an output without a reference script from Init to conviction.

Build every forced-order drill fixture as a native-only transaction

The drill's forced-order families placed a Plutus mint, or an output
carrying a reference script, in their L1 orders. The tx-order mint and the
SDK screen admit only native-only forced transactions, so every forced-order
family failed before its order was signed.

All forced-order fixtures now share one builder: the ledger owner's signed
spend into one protected output, minting one token under an always-true
native policy, with a required signer and the native script witness, and no
redeemer, integrity hash, reference script, auxiliary data or validity upper
bound. The Plutus builder remains only for the validation-trace fixture's
normal L2 transaction. The order submission bytes come from one helper that
the new test also uses.

The new test screens those exact submission bytes through the SDK's
tx-order material derivation, and checks locally that each forced family
still classifies through the full catalogue, prepares its proof, and that
its honest successor is healthy. Two families are held out of that check
pending a ruling.

Read the drill's chain transactions one Ogmios session at a time

Every confirmed-transaction read on an attached stack opens its own
Ogmios chain-sync session, and each session is a new node-to-client
connection to the stack's cardano-node. Callers ask for several reads at
once, and a burst of them overflowed the node's socket backlog: Ogmios
dropped the websockets it could not connect, and the drill failed a family
on "Ogmios chain-sync socket closed".

The reader now runs its reads one at a time, in the order they were asked
for. A failed read rejects only its own caller; the next one still runs.

Resume a completed withdrawal from its recorded payout

A resumed run reconciled every completed step again, and the withdrawal
step proved its payout by finding the payout output unspent at the L1
node's tip. A later cycle's deposit spends that output, so a resume after
cycle 1 waited out the full timeout and failed. Inclusion proven at depth
is permanent: a complete record that holds this withdrawal's payout (same
event, address and assets) is now taken as the proof, and only the L2
spend, the balance guard and readiness are checked again.

Select three more checks from the files they read

Three preflight checks read files their triggers did not name, so a change
to one of those files passed preflight unchecked:

- workflow-lint lints the composite actions under .github/actions/ as well
  as the workflows.
- agent-enforcement-tags resolves [eslint] tags against the ESLint configs,
  [ci] tags against the workflows' step names and [hook] tags against
  .githooks/.
- registry.mjs imports onchain/aiken/scripts/guard-focused-selector.mjs,
  which imports complete-test-shards.mjs, so both are preflight's own code
  and now full-run paths beside scripts/preflight/**.

Closes #947

Select the tooling self-tests from the files they read

repo-tooling-tests ran only on changes under scripts/, .githooks/ and
.claude/settings.json, yet several of its self-tests hold files outside
scripts/ to each other: the journey wiring check reads the watcher journey
tests and Node CI's workflow. A new journey test therefore passed preflight
and failed Repo Tools CI after the push.

Each self-test that reads files outside scripts/ now declares them in
toolingTestInputs, and the step is selected from those declarations. A
change to a declared file runs only the self-tests that read it; a change
under the step's own paths, a full run and `--run repo-tooling-tests` still
run the whole suite.

registry.tooling-inputs.test.mjs pins the selection and runs each declaring
self-test in a copy of the repository holding only scripts/ and the files it
declares, so a read left off its entry fails there, as does a glob that
matches no file. A self-test with no entry at all is not caught: whoever
adds a self-test that reads outside scripts/ adds its entry.

Refs #947

Wait out public DA's not_found after a block commits

The node reports a transfer committed before it hands the block's payload
to the committee, whose store the public retained-DA server reads. The
journey's transfer step fetched that payload once, so a fetch landing in
between failed the run with not_found although the payload arrived seconds
later.

The fetch now asks again while every attempt answers not_found, within the
step's existing limit, reusing one retained-DA runtime, and throws the same
error with the last attempts when the limit runs out. Any other answer
(conflict, invalid content, refusal, failed verification, transport error,
timeout) still fails at once.

Run the new drill harness journey tests in node CI

Five watcher-journey test files added with the drill harness fixes need no
devnet but were missing from the node CI list, so the wiring check failed.

State what an unspent seed row proves at a point

A seed row reads unspent while no spend at or below the point is
recorded. It may also cover an output created after the origin while its
wallet was untracked, so it does not prove the output existed at a point
before its seed slot.
